title: The Eight Sealed In Glass
hook_text: TWO YEARS. ONE DOME. NOT ENOUGH FOOD.

beats.vo: You are eating less than you did at thirty and the weight will not move, darling.
beats.caption: EATING LESS. STILL STUCK.

beats.vo: Eight people were sealed in a glass dome and accidentally proved something about that.
beats.caption: SEALED IN FOR TWO YEARS

beats.vo: Arizona desert, 1991. Biosphere 2, a giant greenhouse locked from the inside.
beats.caption: ARIZONA, 1991

beats.vo: One of the eight was Roy Walford, a gerontologist who studied why bodies age.
beats.caption: A DOCTOR OF OLD AGE

beats.vo: Then the crops failed. The crew dropped to under two thousand calories a day.
beats.caption: THE CROPS FAILED

beats.vo: Walford did not call for help. He started taking blood.
beats.caption: HE TOOK BLOOD INSTEAD

beats.vo: Over two years they lost a tenth to a fifth of their body weight.
beats.caption: A FIFTH OF THEMSELVES

beats.vo: Blood pressure, cholesterol, blood sugar and inflammation all fell to numbers seen in lab animals bred to live long.
beats.caption: NUMBERS FROM LONG-LIVED ANIMALS

beats.vo: It was an accident inside a sealed building, so it was never a proper trial.
beats.caption: AN ACCIDENT, NOT A TRIAL

beats.vo: Eight people is eight people. And they came out thin, tired and arguing.
beats.caption: THEY CAME OUT ARGUING

beats.vo: Eating less without going short on nutrients is still the most repeated life-extension finding in animals.
beats.caption: STILL THE MOST REPEATED FINDING

beats.vo: In humans it has never been proven to extend life, and starving yourself is not the lesson, darling.
beats.caption: NOT PROVEN IN PEOPLE

beats.vo: Your body was not failing you. It was doing exactly what it does when the food runs out.
beats.caption: IT WAS DOING ITS JOB

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

title: The Diet Sealed In A Tomb

beats.vo: Your hunger does not switch off any more, no matter what you take away, darling.
beats.caption: HUNGER THAT NEVER STOPS

beats.vo: Someone wrote a manual about that and had it buried with her.
beats.caption: BURIED WITH HER

beats.vo: Hunan, China, 1973. Archaeologists open Tomb 3 at Mawangdui.
beats.caption: MAWANGDUI, TOMB 3

beats.vo: It had been sealed since 168 BCE for the family of the Marquise of Dai.
beats.caption: SHUT FOR 2,168 YEARS

beats.vo: Inside, on silk, a text called Quegu Shiqi. Eliminating Grain and Eating Qi.
beats.caption: ELIMINATING GRAIN

beats.vo: It is the oldest known diet manual on earth.
beats.caption: THE OLDEST DIET MANUAL

beats.vo: Drop the five grains completely. Live on breath and one specific fern root.
beats.caption: BREATH AND ONE ROOT

beats.vo: The Taoists believed grain fed three worms in the gut that caused hunger, decay and age.
beats.caption: THREE WORMS IN THE GUT

beats.vo: Starve the worms, they wrote, and the body grows light again.
beats.caption: STARVE THEM. GROW LIGHT.

beats.vo: There are no worms. That part is simply wrong.
beats.caption: THERE ARE NO WORMS

beats.vo: But cutting grain and eating in a narrow window is the shape of every modern fasting protocol.
beats.caption: THE SHAPE OF MODERN FASTING

beats.vo: They had the practice twenty-one centuries before anyone had the reason, darling.
beats.caption: PRACTICE BEFORE REASON

beats.vo: Your hunger is not weakness. It is older than the writing that tried to tame it.
beats.caption: OLDER THAN THE WRITING

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-2-168-year-old-diet-found-in-a-tomb)

title: The Old Man And The Syringe

beats.vo: Your strength is leaving quietly and nobody has offered you anything for it, darling.
beats.caption: STRENGTH LEAVING QUIETLY

beats.vo: In 1889 one of Europe's great scientists stood up and said he had fixed that in himself.
beats.caption: HE SAID HE HAD FIXED IT

beats.vo: The first of June, 1889. The Society of Biology in Paris.
beats.caption: PARIS, 1 JUNE 1889

beats.vo: Charles-Edouard Brown-Sequard, seventy-two years old, respected across the continent.
beats.caption: SEVENTY-TWO YEARS OLD

beats.vo: He told the room he had been injecting himself with crushed extract of dog and guinea pig testicles.
beats.caption: HE TOLD THEM WHAT WAS IN IT

beats.vo: His strength was back. His mind was sharp. He felt thirty years younger.
beats.caption: THIRTY YEARS YOUNGER

beats.vo: Europe laughed at him. They laughed for the rest of his life.
beats.caption: EUROPE LAUGHED

beats.vo: They were right to. Modern testing found almost no active hormone in his mixture at all.
beats.caption: ALMOST NO HORMONE IN IT

beats.vo: A seventy-two-year-old man had talked himself young. That is all it was.
beats.caption: HE TALKED HIMSELF YOUNG

beats.vo: But the idea underneath was correct. Hormones fall with age, and restoring them changes how old a body feels.
beats.caption: THE IDEA WAS CORRECT

beats.vo: Medicine needed decades to come back round to what the laughing-stock had said.
beats.caption: DECADES TO COME BACK

beats.vo: He was wrong about his syringe and right about his body, darling.
beats.caption: WRONG SYRINGE. RIGHT BODY.

beats.vo: Being early and being ridiculous have always looked the same from the outside.
beats.caption: EARLY LOOKS LIKE RIDICULOUS

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-72-year-old-who-injected-himself-with-gland-extract)

title: The Chamber Built For Divers

beats.vo: You suspect you are older on the inside than you look on the outside, darling.
beats.caption: OLDER INSIDE THAN OUT

beats.vo: A chamber built for drowning divers was pointed at that question.
beats.caption: BUILT FOR DIVERS

beats.vo: Tel Aviv, 2020. Doctor Shai Efrati takes thirty-five adults, all sixty-four or older.
beats.caption: 35 ADULTS. ALL OVER 64.

beats.vo: Sixty sessions in a pressurised chamber, over ninety days.
beats.caption: 60 SESSIONS IN 90 DAYS

beats.vo: The chambers were designed for divers surfacing too fast, not for old age.
beats.caption: NOT DESIGNED FOR AGE

beats.vo: At the ends of your chromosomes sit caps called telomeres. They shorten each time a cell divides.
beats.caption: CAPS THAT KEEP SHORTENING

beats.vo: They are a clock. Everyone's runs one direction.
beats.caption: A CLOCK THAT RUNS ONE WAY

beats.vo: Blood taken after ninety days showed those caps longer by up to thirty-eight percent.
beats.caption: LONGER BY 38%

beats.vo: Worn-out cells that refuse to die dropped by up to thirty-seven percent.
beats.caption: 37% FEWER WORN-OUT CELLS

beats.vo: Thirty-five people is a small room, and no one has yet shown it means a longer life.
beats.caption: THIRTY-FIVE IS A SMALL ROOM

beats.vo: The oxygen is not the trick. Pressure then release is a controlled stress that makes cells repair.
beats.caption: STRESS, THEN REPAIR

beats.vo: It costs what a car costs, and nobody is giving it away, darling.
beats.caption: IT COSTS WHAT A CAR COSTS

beats.vo: The clock at the end of your chromosomes moved. That was thought impossible.
beats.caption: THE CLOCK MOVED

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-chamber-that-lengthened-telomeres-in-ninety-days)

title: The Root They Patented

beats.vo: You feel old at a level no cream reaches, darling.
beats.caption: DEEPER THAN ANY CREAM

beats.vo: A California company went looking for that level in a Chinese apothecary.
beats.caption: THEY WENT LOOKING IN AN APOTHECARY

beats.vo: The year 2000. Geron Corporation begins screening traditional Chinese medicine extracts.
beats.caption: THE YEAR 2000

beats.vo: They are hunting one thing: something that switches on telomerase.
beats.caption: HUNTING ONE ENZYME

beats.vo: Telomerase rebuilds the caps on your chromosomes that shorten every time a cell divides.
beats.caption: IT REBUILDS THE CAPS

beats.vo: They find it inside astragalus root, used in China for over a thousand years.
beats.caption: INSIDE ASTRAGALUS ROOT

beats.vo: The molecule is cycloastragenol. They patent it.
beats.caption: THEY PATENTED IT

beats.vo: From 2008 it sells as TA-65, at a price no herbalist ever charged.
beats.caption: SOLD AS TA-65

beats.vo: A thousand years in a clay pot, then a patent, then a price.
beats.caption: A PATENT, THEN A PRICE

beats.vo: The same enzyme that keeps a cell young is the one cancer cells switch on to never die.
beats.caption: CANCER USES THE SAME SWITCH

beats.vo: A randomised trial in 2024 found it did measurably lengthen telomeres in people over fifty.
beats.caption: MEASURED IN 2024

beats.vo: The root itself is still sold as tea and powder for almost nothing, darling.
beats.caption: THE ROOT IS STILL CHEAP

beats.vo: They did not discover it. They found it, and put a fence around it.
beats.caption: THEY BUILT A FENCE

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-chinese-herb-the-biotech-company-patented-in-the-year-20)

title: The Hormone Of Being Held

beats.vo: A pulled muscle used to heal in a week and now it takes a season, darling.
beats.caption: A WEEK, NOW A SEASON

beats.vo: The reason may be a hormone you make when someone holds you.
beats.caption: MADE WHEN YOU ARE HELD

beats.vo: Berkeley, 2014. Irina Conboy's lab, working with Christian Elabd and Wendy Cousin.
beats.caption: BERKELEY, 2014

beats.vo: They measured oxytocin in the blood of young mice and old mice.
beats.caption: YOUNG BLOOD, OLD BLOOD

beats.vo: Oxytocin is the bonding hormone. Childbirth, touch, trust.
beats.caption: THE BONDING HORMONE

beats.vo: Young mice carried roughly three times as much of it as the old ones.
beats.caption: THREE TIMES AS MUCH

beats.vo: So they injected the old mice with it and watched the muscle.
beats.caption: THEY INJECTED THE OLD ONES

beats.vo: The muscle stem cells started dividing and repairing like a young animal's again.
beats.caption: OLD STEM CELLS WOKE UP

beats.vo: Oxytocin receptors sit directly on muscle stem cells. Both the hormone and the receptors fall with age.
beats.caption: RECEPTORS SIT ON THE MUSCLE

beats.vo: Nobody was looking there. It was filed under childbirth, not repair.
beats.caption: FILED UNDER CHILDBIRTH

beats.vo: It was mice. Injecting yourself with oxytocin does not do this, and it is not sold for it.
beats.caption: THIS WAS MICE

beats.vo: But it names one quiet reason a tear heals fast at twenty-five and slow at fifty-five.
beats.caption: FAST AT 25. SLOW AT 55.

beats.vo: The hormone of being held turned out to be the hormone of being rebuilt, darling.
beats.caption: HELD, THEN REBUILT

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-cuddle-hormone-that-rebuilt-old-muscle)

title: The Pill That Burned Too Hot

beats.vo: Your metabolism feels like it quietly switched off, darling.
beats.caption: IT SWITCHED OFF

beats.vo: Once, there was a pill that switched it back on. It is also why people died.
beats.caption: AND WHY PEOPLE DIED

beats.vo: French munitions factories, the First World War. Workers handling one chemical grew hot and thin.
beats.caption: HOT AND THIN AT THE FACTORY

beats.vo: Some of them also died of it, right there at the bench.
beats.caption: SOME DIED AT THE BENCH

beats.vo: Summer of 1933. Three Stanford scientists put a number on it.
beats.caption: STANFORD, 1933

beats.vo: It sped up human metabolism by thirty to fifty percent.
beats.caption: METABOLISM UP 30-50%

beats.vo: It went on drugstore counters across America as a diet pill.
beats.caption: ON THE DRUGSTORE COUNTER

beats.vo: Inside your cells, mitochondria turn food into fuel. This let that energy leak out as pure heat.
beats.caption: ENERGY LEAKING AS HEAT

beats.vo: You burn fat simply to stay warm. It is the most direct proof on record that mitochondria set the burn.
beats.caption: MITOCHONDRIA SET THE BURN

beats.vo: There is no dose that is warm and safe. The line between thin and cooked from the inside is thin itself.
beats.caption: NO SAFE DOSE

beats.vo: The FDA banned it in 1938. People still buy it online and people still die of it every year.
beats.caption: BANNED 1938. STILL KILLING.

beats.vo: Do not go looking for this one. It was pulled for working too well in the worst direction.
beats.caption: DO NOT GO LOOKING

beats.vo: Your engine is real and it can be moved. That was never the problem, darling.
beats.caption: THE ENGINE IS REAL

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-diet-pill-that-burned-too-hot)

title: The Lamp Running Out Of Oil
hook_text: PERSIA, 11TH CENTURY. A LAMP, NOT A WOUND.

beats.vo: You sleep, you eat, and still something inside is running down, darling.
beats.caption: STILL RUNNING DOWN

beats.vo: A Persian physician described that exact feeling a thousand years ago.
beats.caption: DESCRIBED A THOUSAND YEARS AGO

beats.vo: Ibn Sina. In the west they called him Avicenna.
beats.caption: IBN SINA

beats.vo: His Canon of Medicine taught doctors from Persia to Europe for six hundred years.
beats.caption: TAUGHT FOR 600 YEARS

beats.vo: He wrote that every body is born with a fixed reserve. He called it radical moisture.
beats.caption: A FIXED RESERVE

beats.vo: He compared it to the oil in a lamp. The flame is your own inner heat.
beats.caption: OIL IN A LAMP

beats.vo: The flame burns the oil. When the oil is gone the light goes out. Nothing refills it.
beats.caption: NOTHING REFILLS IT

beats.vo: So he wrote a section on old age about lowering the flame.
beats.caption: LOWER THE FLAME

beats.vo: Smaller meals taken more often. Gentler days. Warm oil massage after bathing.
beats.caption: SMALLER MEALS. WARM OIL.

beats.vo: There is no radical moisture. The idea was replaced and mostly forgotten.
beats.caption: THERE IS NO SUCH FLUID

beats.vo: But he was arguing that ageing is a burn rate, not an injury.
beats.caption: A BURN RATE, NOT AN INJURY

beats.vo: Which is close to how the slow-metabolism, low-stress work reads today, darling.
beats.caption: CLOSE TO WHAT WE SAY NOW

beats.vo: He could not stop the flame. He simply refused to waste the oil.
beats.caption: HE REFUSED TO WASTE IT

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-doctor-who-said-old-age-is-a-lamp-running-out-of-oil)

title: The Empress And The Cave
hook_text: CLIMBED FOR IT. FED TO AN EMPRESS.

beats.vo: Your face has lost its plumpness and sleep is not giving it back, darling.
beats.caption: SLEEP DOES NOT GIVE IT BACK

beats.vo: An empress ate a bird's saliva every morning for exactly this.
beats.caption: A BIRD'S SALIVA. EVERY MORNING.

beats.vo: Limestone caves across Southeast Asia. Harvesters climb sheer walls in the dark.
beats.caption: CLIMBING IN THE DARK

beats.vo: They are after swiftlet nests, built almost entirely of the bird's own hardened spit.
beats.caption: NESTS MADE OF SPIT

beats.vo: For a thousand years the harvest went to the Chinese imperial court and nowhere else.
beats.caption: RESERVED FOR THE COURT

beats.vo: The Empress Dowager Cixi is said to have taken it as part of her beauty routine.
beats.caption: EMPRESS DOWAGER CIXI

beats.vo: She was known into old age for a face that had not moved with her years.
beats.caption: A FACE THAT DID NOT MOVE

beats.vo: The nests are dense in sialic-acid glycopeptides. Protein fragments studded with sugars.
beats.caption: PROTEIN STUDDED WITH SUGAR

beats.vo: Your body uses that exact class of molecule for skin repair and cell signalling.
beats.caption: USED FOR SKIN REPAIR

beats.vo: A court was eating a peptide centuries before anyone had the word peptide.
beats.caption: BEFORE THE WORD EXISTED

beats.vo: It has never been properly trialled for skin, and it is one of the costliest foods on earth.
beats.caption: NEVER PROPERLY TRIALLED

beats.vo: Men still die falling off those cave walls for it, darling.
beats.caption: MEN STILL FALL FOR IT

beats.vo: She was not eating a delicacy. She was eating building material.
beats.caption: SHE ATE BUILDING MATERIAL

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-empress-who-ate-cave-spit-every-morning)

title: Minus One Hundred And Sixty-Six

beats.vo: You are stiffer than you were and you move like something that needs oiling, darling.
beats.caption: YOU MOVE LIKE IT NEEDS OILING

beats.vo: A doctor in Japan decided the answer was to make you much, much colder.
beats.caption: MUCH, MUCH COLDER

beats.vo: Oita, Japan, 1978. Doctor Toshima Yamaguchi builds a chamber.
beats.caption: OITA, JAPAN, 1978

beats.vo: His patients have rheumatoid arthritis. Their joints are swollen and will not settle.
beats.caption: JOINTS THAT WILL NOT SETTLE

beats.vo: He chills the air inside to roughly minus one hundred and sixty-six degrees.
beats.caption: MINUS 166 DEGREES

beats.vo: Then he puts them in it. For a few minutes at a time.
beats.caption: A FEW MINUTES AT A TIME

beats.vo: The cold is not treating the joint. It is a shock, deliberately given.
beats.caption: A SHOCK, DELIBERATELY GIVEN

beats.vo: Cells read a hard brief stress as a threat and switch into repair.
beats.caption: STRESS READ AS A THREAT

beats.vo: Mitochondria answer it by building sturdier versions of themselves for the next one.
beats.caption: THEY BUILD BACK STURDIER

beats.vo: The trick is that it ends. A long cold does damage. A short one gives an order.
beats.caption: THE TRICK IS THAT IT ENDS

beats.vo: It became a luxury service, sold by the session in cities that never saw Oita.
beats.caption: SOLD BY THE SESSION

beats.vo: A cold shower is free and reaches the same signal, darling.
beats.caption: A COLD SHOWER IS FREE

beats.vo: He was not numbing anything. He was giving the body a reason to rebuild.
beats.caption: A REASON TO REBUILD

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-japanese-doctor-who-froze-the-pain-away-in-oita)

title: The Tank Full Of Infants

beats.vo: You do not want the damage slowed. You want it undone, darling.
beats.caption: NOT SLOWED. UNDONE.

beats.vo: One animal on this earth actually does that, and a student found it by accident.
beats.caption: ONE ANIMAL ACTUALLY DOES

beats.vo: Rapallo, Italy, 1988. A marine biology student named Christian Sommer.
beats.caption: RAPALLO, ITALY, 1988

beats.vo: He is keeping a tiny jellyfish, Turritopsis dohrnii, in a lab tank.
beats.caption: ONE TINY JELLYFISH

beats.vo: He expects the adults to age and die, because that is what animals do.
beats.caption: HE EXPECTED THEM TO DIE

beats.vo: He comes back and the tank is full of infants again.
beats.caption: THE TANK WAS FULL OF INFANTS

beats.vo: Injure or starve this jellyfish and its adult cells collapse and reorganise.
beats.caption: ADULT CELLS COLLAPSE

beats.vo: They go back to the infant polyp stage, then grow into a new adult with the same genes.
beats.caption: BACK TO THE BEGINNING

beats.vo: Your cells lock into one final identity. A skin cell dies a skin cell.
beats.caption: YOURS LOCK IN. HERS DO NOT.

beats.vo: Its cells never lock. They can go blank and start over.
beats.caption: THEY CAN GO BLANK

beats.vo: It is not immortal. It gets eaten, like everything in the sea.
beats.caption: IT STILL GETS EATEN

beats.vo: And nothing about it transfers to a human body, so beware anyone selling you it, darling.
beats.caption: NOTHING TRANSFERS TO YOU

beats.vo: It does not repair the damage. It refuses to keep the record of it.
beats.caption: IT KEEPS NO RECORD

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-jellyfish-that-turned-back-into-a-baby)

title: The Molecule In The Meat

beats.vo: Your joints and your skin have started to set, like something left out too long, darling.
beats.caption: SOMETHING LEFT OUT TOO LONG

beats.vo: There is a word for what is doing that, and it is closer to caramel than to rust.
beats.caption: CLOSER TO CARAMEL THAN RUST

beats.vo: Kharkov University, Ukraine, 1900. Two chemists are pulling apart plain meat extract.
beats.caption: KHARKOV, 1900

beats.vo: Vladimir Gulewitsch and Sergei Amiradzibi isolate a small molecule and name it carnosine.
beats.caption: THEY NAMED IT CARNOSINE

beats.vo: It sits there in the literature for a century, unremarkable.
beats.caption: A CENTURY OF NOTHING

beats.vo: Then researchers start taking apart the naked mole rat.
beats.caption: THEN THE MOLE RAT

beats.vo: It lives past thirty years. A mouse of the same size gets three.
beats.caption: THIRTY YEARS. A MOUSE GETS THREE.

beats.vo: Its tissue is packed with unusually high concentrations of carnosine.
beats.caption: PACKED WITH IT

beats.vo: Sugar in your blood quietly glues itself onto proteins in your skin, arteries and joints.
beats.caption: SUGAR GLUES ONTO PROTEIN

beats.vo: Decade by decade, tissue that used to be flexible sets hard. Carnosine appears to block that.
beats.caption: FLEXIBLE TISSUE SETS HARD

beats.vo: Nobody could patent a molecule found in meat in 1900, so nobody funded it.
beats.caption: NOBODY COULD PATENT MEAT

beats.vo: It is concentrated in muscle meat and sold as a supplement, and the human evidence is thin, darling.
beats.caption: THE HUMAN EVIDENCE IS THIN

beats.vo: The animal built to outlive its own size class is full of it. That is not proof. It is a direction.
beats.caption: NOT PROOF. A DIRECTION.

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-molecule-hiding-in-the-longest-lived-rodent-alive)

title: A Rope And A Short Blade

beats.vo: You are winded on the stairs now and you know exactly when that started, darling.
beats.caption: WINDED ON THE STAIRS

beats.vo: On a mountain in Japan there are men who decided that would never happen to them.
beats.caption: THEY DECIDED OTHERWISE

beats.vo: Mount Hiei, near Kyoto. Tendai Buddhist monks. The practice is called kaihogyo.
beats.caption: MOUNT HIEI, KYOTO

beats.vo: One thousand days of running and walking, spread across seven years.
beats.caption: 1,000 DAYS. 7 YEARS.

beats.vo: Roughly twenty-four thousand miles. Near enough around the earth.
beats.caption: AROUND THE EARTH

beats.vo: Each circuit stops to pray at some two hundred and sixty shrines.
beats.caption: 260 SHRINES A CIRCUIT

beats.vo: Every monk carries a rope and a short blade.
beats.caption: A ROPE AND A BLADE

beats.vo: They are for him. Tradition holds that a monk who cannot finish does not come down.
beats.caption: THEY ARE FOR HIM

beats.vo: Since 1885, forty-six men have completed it.
beats.caption: FORTY-SIX SINCE 1885

beats.vo: This is not exercise and it is not for you. It is a religious vow with a death clause.
beats.caption: A VOW WITH A DEATH CLAUSE

beats.vo: But the shape underneath is the least glamorous finding in the whole field.
beats.caption: THE LEAST GLAMOROUS FINDING

beats.vo: Daily movement, sustained for years, is the only thing that reliably rebuilds the engine, darling.
beats.caption: DAILY. FOR YEARS.

beats.vo: They did not train to run. They trained so the body would not run down.
beats.caption: SO IT WOULD NOT RUN DOWN

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-monks-who-ran-24-000-miles-to-never-grow-tired)

title: The Cells That Ate Themselves

beats.vo: You are carrying a heaviness that sleep does not clear, darling.
beats.caption: SLEEP DOES NOT CLEAR IT

beats.vo: A man in Tokyo watched cells take out their own rubbish and won a Nobel for it.
beats.caption: HE WATCHED THEM TAKE OUT THE RUBBISH

beats.vo: Tokyo Institute of Technology, 1988. Yoshinori Ohsumi at a microscope.
beats.caption: TOKYO, 1988

beats.vo: He is looking at yeast cells he has deliberately starved.
beats.caption: DELIBERATELY STARVED

beats.vo: They begin eating their own insides. Not falling apart. Orderly. On purpose.
beats.caption: ORDERLY. ON PURPOSE.

beats.vo: Damaged proteins, worn-out parts, decades of debris, all broken down and reused.
beats.caption: DEBRIS BROKEN DOWN AND REUSED

beats.vo: The process is called autophagy. Self-eating.
beats.caption: AUTOPHAGY. SELF-EATING.

beats.vo: It slows down as you age, and that slowdown is now read as a central driver of looking old.
beats.caption: IT SLOWS AS YOU AGE

beats.vo: In 2016 he was given the Nobel Prize in Medicine.
beats.caption: THE NOBEL, 2016

beats.vo: Buddhist monks and Ramadan fasters had been running the practice for fourteen centuries.
beats.caption: FOURTEEN CENTURIES OF PRACTICE

beats.vo: They had no word for it and no microscope. They just had the fast.
beats.caption: NO WORD. NO MICROSCOPE.

beats.vo: Twelve hours or more without food appears to start it, though the human measurements are still rough, darling.
beats.caption: TWELVE HOURS OR MORE

beats.vo: The prize was for the explanation. The practice was never lost.
beats.caption: THE PRACTICE WAS NEVER LOST

script.source: writing-agent v3 (Shalev shape; Director assigns clips)

notes: batch 5, owner-picked from the long list (the-nobel-prize-the-fasting-monks-already-knew)

title: Ten Days To A New Coat

beats.vo: Your hair is thinner, your skin does not spring back, and nothing you buy touches it, darling.
beats.caption: NOTHING YOU BUY TOUCHES IT

beats.vo: There are cells in you that stopped working years ago and refuse to leave.
beats.caption: THEY REFUSE TO LEAVE

beats.vo: Rotterdam, 2017. Erasmus University Medical Center. A biologist called Peter de Keizer.
beats.caption: ROTTERDAM, 2017

beats.vo: He builds a peptide and names it FOXO4-DRI.
beats.caption: HE BUILT FOXO4-DRI

beats.vo: His mice are old. Dull coats, balding, patchy.
beats.caption: DULL, BALDING, PATCHY

beats.vo: Ten days of injections. The mice grow back a full glossy coat.
beats.caption: TEN DAYS TO A FULL COAT

beats.vo: The dead-but-not-dying cells leak inflammation into everything around them.
beats.caption: THEY LEAK INFLAMMATION

beats.vo: That leak is a real part of why skin sags, hair thins and joints stiffen.
beats.caption: WHY SKIN SAGS

beats.vo: Those cells survive by holding two proteins together, FOXO4 and p53.
beats.caption: TWO PROTEINS, HELD TOGETHER

beats.vo: De Keizer's peptide found that exact handshake and prised it apart.
beats.caption: HE PRISED THEM APART

beats.vo: The cells finally received the order to self-destruct. That was all it took.
beats.caption: THE ORDER FINALLY ARRIVED

beats.vo: This was mice, in 2017, and it is not a human treatment. Anyone selling you it is selling you a mouse study, darling.
beats.caption: IT IS STILL A MOUSE STUDY

beats.vo: Your body was not refusing to repair. It was being shouted over.
beats.caption: IT WAS BEING SHOUTED OVER

title: The Rats Who Danced

beats.vo: Your engine gave up before your mind was ready to, darling.
beats.caption: THE ENGINE GAVE UP FIRST

beats.vo: A Berkeley biochemist wrote one sentence about old rats that nobody has forgotten.
beats.caption: ONE SENTENCE ABOUT OLD RATS

beats.vo: Bruce Ames, University of California, Berkeley.
beats.caption: BRUCE AMES, BERKELEY

beats.vo: His rats are twenty-four to twenty-eight months old. In a person that is seventy-five to eighty.
beats.caption: SEVENTY-FIVE IN HUMAN YEARS

beats.vo: They are slow, dull and finished.
beats.caption: SLOW, DULL, FINISHED

beats.vo: He feeds them two molecules for one month. Acetyl-L-carnitine and alpha-lipoic acid.
beats.caption: TWO MOLECULES. ONE MONTH.

beats.vo: Published in 2002. His own words in the write-up:
beats.caption: PUBLISHED 2002

beats.vo: These old rats got up and did the Macarena.
beats.caption: THEY DID THE MACARENA

beats.vo: Inside every cell, mitochondria hold a voltage across a membrane. That is how they make energy.
beats.caption: A VOLTAGE ACROSS A MEMBRANE

beats.vo: Old mitochondria leak. The voltage drops and the power plant runs at half.
beats.caption: OLD ONES LEAK

beats.vo: The two molecules recharge them directly. The rats did not get younger. Their engines did.
beats.caption: THE ENGINES GOT YOUNGER

beats.vo: Both are sold cheaply as supplements, and the human results have never matched the rats, darling.
beats.caption: HUMANS NEVER MATCHED IT

beats.vo: Nobody remembers the mechanism. Everybody remembers the Macarena.
beats.caption: EVERYBODY REMEMBERS THE DANCE

title: The Men Paid To Get Fat

beats.vo: You fight for the last few pounds and your body puts them straight back, darling.
beats.caption: IT PUTS THEM STRAIGHT BACK

beats.vo: In 1967 a doctor paid prisoners to prove that was not your fault.
beats.caption: HE PAID THEM TO PROVE IT

beats.vo: Vermont State Prison. The physician is Ethan Sims, University of Vermont.
beats.caption: VERMONT STATE PRISON

beats.vo: The inmates are paid to do one thing. Eat as much as they possibly can.
beats.caption: EAT AS MUCH AS YOU CAN

beats.vo: Some are putting away upward of ten thousand calories a day.
beats.caption: 10,000 CALORIES A DAY

beats.vo: For two hundred straight days.
beats.caption: 200 STRAIGHT DAYS

beats.vo: Most of them could not get past twenty or twenty-five pounds.
beats.caption: THEY COULD NOT GET PAST 25 LB

beats.vo: Their own metabolic rates sped up, as if defending the weight they started at.
beats.caption: THEIR ENGINES SPED UP

beats.vo: Then Sims let them eat normally again.
beats.caption: THEN HE LET THEM STOP

beats.vo: The weight came off in about ten weeks. Nobody tried. It simply went.
beats.caption: TEN WEEKS. NOBODY TRIED.

beats.vo: This is the set point. A weight the body defends in both directions.
beats.caption: DEFENDED BOTH DIRECTIONS

beats.vo: It runs as hard against gaining as it does against losing, which is no comfort at all, darling.
beats.caption: IT FIGHTS BOTH WAYS

beats.vo: You have not been failing to hold a line. You have been arguing with one.
beats.caption: YOU WERE ARGUING WITH A LINE

title: The Ball In The Olive Oil

beats.vo: You are tired in a way that feels less like sleep and more like rust, darling.
beats.caption: LESS LIKE SLEEP. MORE LIKE RUST.

beats.vo: In 2012 some rats in France were given olive oil and lived nearly twice as long.
beats.caption: NEARLY TWICE AS LONG

beats.vo: The molecule is C60. Sixty carbon atoms in a hollow cage.
beats.caption: SIXTY CARBON ATOMS

beats.vo: It is shaped like a tiny football. Finding it won a Nobel Prize on its own.
beats.caption: SHAPED LIKE A FOOTBALL

beats.vo: French researchers dissolve it into ordinary olive oil and feed tiny doses for life.
beats.caption: DISSOLVED IN OLIVE OIL

beats.vo: The treated rats live nearly double the untreated ones.
beats.caption: THE RATS LIVED DOUBLE

beats.vo: It runs in Biomaterials in 2012 and then almost nothing happens.
beats.caption: THEN ALMOST NOTHING

beats.vo: Your mitochondria make energy and throw off free radicals as exhaust.
beats.caption: FREE RADICALS AS EXHAUST

beats.vo: That exhaust is tied to the wear that shows up as age. C60 appears to soak up an extraordinary amount of it.
beats.caption: IT SOAKS UP THE EXHAUST

beats.vo: But the molecule could not be patented in any form a drug company wanted.
beats.caption: NO PATENT WORTH HAVING

beats.vo: So no funding arrived. A near-doubling of rat lifespan, and the field moved on.
beats.caption: THE FIELD MOVED ON

beats.vo: It went to the grey market instead, sold in bottles by people answering to nobody, darling.
beats.caption: SOLD BY PEOPLE ANSWERING TO NOBODY

beats.vo: It was never disproved. It was never funded. Those are different things.
beats.caption: NEVER DISPROVED. NEVER FUNDED.
